chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 296: Li Huowang Tries to Teach the Black Tai Sui to Speak
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang discovers the Black Tai Sui inside him only knows a few overheard words. He crafts a bizarre plan to teach it to read, then finally meets his mysterious handler face-to-face.
og_description: Li Huowang realizes the monster in his gut can't talk. His plan? Lesson one: the alphabet. Then a masked man shows him unexpected kindness.
twitter_description: Li Huowang tries to teach a silent horror to read, and gets a warm reception from the Supervisory Heavenly Office’s biggest fan. It’s almost… nice.

lore_anchors.definition: The empire’s shadowy agency for policing rogue cultivators and managing supernatural calamities. Li Huowang’s employer and potential lifeline.
A pill that contains or represents ‘yang life,’ the user’s vital years. They are a tangible currency in the Dao-Twisted World, usable for payment or as a ‘security deposit’ for risky tasks.
A grotesque, parasitic entity that lives inside Li Huowang to suppress his hallucinations. It is currently mute and can only repeat overheard words.
A rotund, smiling man who serves as the Big-Headed Doll, Li Huowang’s handler in the Supervisory Heavenly Office. His surname is historically prestigious.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Black Tai Sui only saying simple words?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because it only knows the words it overheard Li Huowang teaching to Lü Xiucai. It doesn't understand their meaning; it is simply parroting sounds.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang decide to teach it?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He can't get rid of the Black Tai Sui (it suppresses his visions), and he can't kill it without harming himself. Teaching it to speak is the only long-term way to gain a controllable ally instead of a silent passenger.
Li Huowang assumes it's an act, but the gesture itself—returning the pills, offering his name, inviting trust—is more warmth than he's received in months. For now, it's a welcome reprieve.
